newsitem.title: USA: Newmont excluding no options on Santa Fe.
newsitem.headline: Newmont excluding no options on Santa Fe.

text.p: Newmont Mining Corp chairman Ronald Cambre said Thursday Newmont has not ruled out any options regarding its unsolicited bid to take over Santa Fe Pacific Gold Corp in a stock swap worth over $2 billion.

In a conference call with investors and analysts detailing Newmont's surprise move, Cambre also said he is willing to discuss a friendly deal with Santa Fe, which has yet to respond to the bid made this morning.
Cambre decline to say if the companies were in earlier merger negotiations, or if Newmont was prepared to raise its offer if Santa Fe agreed to negotiate a transaction.
Cambre said part of the rationale for the deal is that the companies' global operations are almost "mirror images" of each other, except for Newmont's Indonesia operation.
A combination would lead to saving in exploration, general and adminstrative expenses, he said.

Specifically, Newmont and Santa Fe operations would complement each other in Central Asia, particularly in Uzbekistan, South America with a combination of Newmont's Peru operations with Santa Fe's work in Brazil, and most significantly -- Nevada.
Merger-related savings in Nevada would start at $40 million per year, he said, noting there is "potential for significant savings" in the expected overlap of employees working in the state.
Newmont has about 2,200 to 2,300 Nevada employees, while Santa Fe has about 1,300 to 1,500, he said.
Terms of the deal call for the exchange of stock at a ratio of 0.33 Newmont shares for each Santa Fe share.
Cambre said the bid does not include a collar on share prices that would trigger renegotiation of the terms if the stocks' made sharp moves up or down.
In response to a listener question on the absense of a share-price collar, Cambre said: "All gold stock prices are depressed because the price of gold is depressed. The whole group is undervalued."
He added that Newmont does not own any shares in Santa Fe, and said that the pooling-of-interest aspect of the proposed transaction is a necessary part of any deal.

Pooling of interest is the line-by-line combination of merged companies' financials that allows for tax-free accounting, as opposed to purhcase accounting which typically results in significant goodwill-related charges.
In an interview with Reuters after the conference call, Cambre said the main reason behind the bid's timing is that as as of October 1, Newmont could use pooling of interest in its proposal.
The date was roughly the two-year anniversary of Santa Fe's spin off from what is now Burlington Northern Santa Fe Corp.
Newmont shares finished Thursday trade at 47-1/8, off 3/8, which values each Santa Fe share at $15.55.
Santa Fe shares finished trade at 14-7/8, or $14.875, up three.
